previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for his 25th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of reinduction therapy. He presented electively in stable condition and received methotrexate 8 g/m² with urinary alkalinization. Temozolomide 240 mg daily was continued on a 7-day on/7-day off cycle. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.17, and he tolerated treatment without complications. Sodium remained stable, and no adjustments were needed to desmopressin. He reported increased depressive symptoms, prompting a psychiatry clinic referral. He was discharged home with instructions to continue leucovorin and bicarbonate for 24 hours, resume all home medications, and follow up for Rituxan and MRI surveillance in one month.
